assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and molecular sieves with controlled pore topology, composition and active sites (organic structure-directing agents, Ti/Sn/Al framework sites, new topologies) underpins refining, petrochemicals, emissions control and selective oxidation. Original, clear, with decisive industrial and academic impact; structure-to-function logic is exactly what the field has shown.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalytic design and industrial transfer), Davis (design and synthesis of new framework materials) and Zones (structure-directing agents, Chevron) give a coherent three-way split of design, synthesis and application. Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis are strong but contribute along a more incremental line; the split is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation in large-scale industrial practice; the field is stable and the recognition is well timed, not premature.
uncertainties: As a structural chemist working on zeolites I may favor this field; the allocation among many deserving people is unresolved.
Some of my knowledge of exact priority claims is uncertain and not independently verified.
Whether the committee sees this as one discovery or a broad field is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cells from a few percent to over 25 percent efficiency in a decade, a remarkable materials-science story with a huge community and clear originality in the use of a defect-tolerant, solution-processable semiconductor.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first reported the perovskite sensitized cell, Grätzel and Park pushed the solid-state architecture and Snaith demonstrated the thin-film, high-efficiency device. Kanatzidis, Park and Seok also have strong claims, so a three-person cut is contested and arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is confirmed independently and widely; long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial scale-up remain unresolved. Timing is arguably still early for real-world impact, though the scientific impact is established.
uncertainties: Operational stability and commercialization are unproven.
Allocation among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis is genuinely disputed.
Grätzel overlaps with the dye-sensitized cell candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns small molecules into hijackers of the ubiquitin-proteasome system, opening previously undruggable targets; the concept is original and has produced clinical candidates. The thalidomide-cereblon molecular-glue story adds mechanistic depth.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept, Ciulli contributed structure-guided design and VHL ligands, and Handa/Ito explain the cereblon mechanism. A fair configuration is possible but excludes several important contributors, so credit is complex.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is emerging but no approved PROTAC yet as far as I know, and I am uncertain on the current state. The chemical concept is well replicated, though recognition may be a bit early.
uncertainties: Clinical outcomes still maturing.
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be recognized together is unclear.
Attribution among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa, Ito and others is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers lets structures be determined from micro- and nanocrystals before radiation damage and enables time-resolved structural movies. It strongly resonates with my interest in enabling methods for small crystals, and it has transformed how reactions are visualized.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the diffract-before-destroy concept and methods, Fromme and colleagues pioneered the sample delivery and first protein experiments, and Schlichting contributed time-resolved applications. Hajdu, an originator of the concept, is not a candidate in my selected set given uncertainty about his status.
assessment.maturity: Method is demonstrated and replicated at several facilities; the range of new chemistry-defining results is still growing, so impact is solid but not yet as broad as the older methods.
uncertainties: Whether the credited set properly captures the originators is uncertain.
Chemistry versus physics or biology placement.
Access limited to a few facilities.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a general, widely used synthetic reaction in pharmaceuticals and materials; mechanistic clarity and ligand design were decisive. Strongly lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently built the general catalytic method and ligand families; Kosugi's earlier tin amide work is a precursor. Two laureates would be natural, but Pd cross-coupling was recognized in 2010, raising a scope-overlap question.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent use and no stability concerns; timing is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: The 2010 cross-coupling prize may make the committee reluctant.
Kosugi's precursor credit and Migita's earlier work leave some priority ambiguity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The structures and mechanism of nitrogenase reveal how the FeMo cofactor reduces N2, a central problem in bioinorganic and structural chemistry with agricultural significance. Structural determinations provide direct evidence that I value.
assessment.attribution: Rees determined the first structures and the central cofactor interstitial atom with Einsle, while Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe contributed biochemical and cofactor work. The configuration is difficult and the catalytic mechanism is not fully resolved.
assessment.maturity: Structure is established and confirmed; the actual catalytic mechanism still has open questions, so maturity is partial.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 binding and reduction remains debated.
Allocation among structural and biochemical contributors is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Template-directed ordered mesoporous silica (M41S/MCM-41, SBA-15) introduced liquid-crystal templating for tunable mesopores and spawned a large family of porous materials with applications in catalysis, adsorption and delivery.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck at Mobil made the original discovery, Ryoo extended it to carbons and metals, and Stucky and Zhao developed SBA-type materials; Inagaki's FSM-16 is an important parallel claim. Priority is plausible but not simple.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed with long-standing use, though industrial impact is narrower than that of zeolites. Recognition would be late but not premature.
uncertainties: Parallel Japanese and Mobil discoveries complicate credit.
Impact may be less transformative than other porous-material candidates.
My field proximity could bias my assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large, original family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides with tunable surface chemistry, showing strong results for energy storage and electronics. Many compositions and structures have been characterized.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Barsoum and Gogotsi reported the first Ti3C2 MXene with a clear, small, plausible team of three, and Drexel collaboration is the core.
assessment.maturity: Field is young, and applications and reproducibility across labs are still maturing; structural characterization of surface terminations remains challenging. Possibly premature.
uncertainties: Surface termination structure remains hard to determine rigorously.
Practical impact is not yet proven.
Timing may be early.
